chapter: Failure in St. Louis and the Omaha bands
title: First band job in St. Louis flops: could not read fast enough
summary: Thompson joined a St. Louis band replacing a good reading pianist, failed because he could not read fast enough, took an administrative discharge and got his first blues.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: Well, now, tell me, I'm very eager to hear about the first band and how it happened, how it worked.
I might say. Yes. It was my first

attempt and it was completely flopped. But however it was also a great lesson for me not only in music but in life, because I wasn't prepared, and I found out that I wasn't prepared very soon. Now, the band leader was mad at the piano player. he had working for him, who was very, very good. He was a good piano player, he was educated, and he played good music, and he wrote arrangements. Which could be the reason why I was challenged to learn all these things later.
And I went to St. Louis and to join this band. But when I got there I couldn't read music fast enough because I hadn't had the training.

I hadn't had the training and the experience. And at that time you had to read the notes, you know, they had the notes and there was a lot of notes to read. And I hadn't had experience. A young guy. In other words I wasn't good enough, let's put it that way. Just frankly.
Well, now I didn't know this, and the band leader didn't know it, because he didn't try me out ahead of time. And all he knew was I could play, that I could play.
You know, ad lib solos. Which was important. But that wasn't the most important thing, see. And

so I sort of jumped the gun and I gave up my position as a clerk typist in the army, which I got an administrative discharge to accept better employment. That was the legal reading of my papers, of my discharge, in other words, you know; in other words there were several types of discharges. The honorable discharge was the ordinary discharge of the army for ordinary purposes, you know, and then of course there were dishonorable discharges for unpleasant things, in fact I remember making out several dishonorable discharges which had to do with the behavior of some of the men in the army, which wasn't desirable.

You know? But mine was known as an administrative discharge, because I was leaving my position to accept other employment. And so I left the CC camp and went to St. Louis, and that's where I first got my blues, my taste of the blues. (Singing).
Yes, your first blues are very blue, aren't they?
Yes, don't you know it. It's like a woman's first love going sour, you know?
You think a man loves you like you love him, you find out he don't care that much at all. My goodness gracious, I've got the blues, I've got the blues so bad.
